page: Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is driven by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 virtual cores with hyperthreading enabled. It incorporates 320 MB of shared L3 cache and advanced instruction extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Compute capabilities are coupled with 512 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8 GB allocation per virtual core.

A central component of this instance profile is its bundled local high-throughput storage, featuring 15,000 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD space alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate competitive multi-threaded performance, with Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% (21,127.0) and PassMark CPU throughput reaching 78,637.66. Memory bandwidth tests reveal large-block read transfers of 287.15 GB/sec and write transfers of 120.62 GB/sec.

Storage and transaction benchmarks highlight high operational efficiency for disk-heavy environments, recording 87.75 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 106.15 GB/sec. CPU-bound matrix extensions also support intermediate machine learning inferencing, delivering 287.17 tokens per second on prompt processing for 7B models. However, without dedicated GPU acceleration, larger parameter models encounter generation throughput constraints.

From an operational cost perspective, the instance balances intensive I/O throughput against broad system compute, mitigating external network storage transfer costs through its dense 15 TB NVMe array. Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is strategically suited for high-IOPS relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, massive caching layers, large-scale search engines, and data analytics pipelines requiring immediate access to high-capacity local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz on the AWS Nitro system. The server includes 512 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, 320 MB of L3 cache, and a large bundled local storage pool of 15,000 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 38 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware accelerators include Intel AMX and AVX-512 for accelerated vectorized computation. In performance testing, the instance achieved top-tier Geekbench results (2,299 single-core and 21,127 multi-core) and processed 87.75 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking discrete GPUs, its high memory density and extensive direct-attached NVMe storage deliver strong I/O efficiency without external disk overhead, making it best matched for intensive database engines, distributed NoSQL clusters, search indices, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
